description: Today's artificial intelligence models can predict whether someone with a genetic change will develop a disease, but cannot answer two critical questions: Why did the disease occur, and how do we design a treatment?
title: AI virtual cell technology could reveal how genetic changes and drugs alter cells

description: Structured light has become an important tool across modern optics. By shaping properties such as amplitude, phase, polarization and spatial mode, researchers can create light fields with capabilities beyond those of conventional laser beams. These engineered light fields are finding applications in communications, imaging, sensing, optical computing and quantum photonics. However, many structured-light systems still rely on multiple discrete optical components that require careful alignment and occupy significant space.
title: Building structured-light systems in three dimensions

description: On an early October morning, as MBARI's research vessel Paragon left Moss Landing with three robots loaded on its deck, Monterey Bay was showing off.
title: Innovative technology offers a bold new vision for monitoring ocean health

description: Botanists have described a new Ophiopogon species from the Yunnan Wenshan National Nature Reserve in southeastern China. They named it Ophiopogon longiscapus for its unusually long flowering stalk, or scape.
title: New mondo grass species found in Yunnan

description: Accepting the Republican nomination for president in 1964, Barry Goldwater declared, "I would remind you that extremism in the defense of liberty is no vice!" His statement illustrates how the cause being defended can shape judgments about the actions taken in its name.
title: Organizational science offers new lens for studying extremism

description: The last bird to go extinct in Aotearoa New Zealand was a tiny wren that disappeared from a small island off the southern tip of Rakiura Stewart Island around 1972.
title: New study: The last bird to go extinct in NZ has lessons for saving other species

description: Climate change is a global reality, but people often encounter it through different local realities. For some, it enters everyday life through social media feeds, news reports, scientific findings and public discussion. For others, it is through water scarcity, food insecurity, floods, heat waves, wildfires or the loss of a home or a loved one.
title: Climate communication that resonates must be based on empathy

description: The U.S. Naval Research Laboratory-developed Navy Environmental Prediction sysTem Utilizing a Nonhydrostatic Engine, known as NEPTUNE, is poised to become an operational Navy weather prediction capability, providing improved environmental forecasts to support naval operations around the globe.
title: NEPTUNE poised to replace Navy's global weather model, improving forecasts over open ocean

description: A week before Hurricane Melissa slammed into Jamaica last fall, the forecast models couldn't agree on where it was headed or how strong it would get. One got it right—an AI model from Google DeepMind, which called both the storm's path and its Category 5 strength.
title: Putting Google's AI hurricane model to the test

description: AI companions could help reduce loneliness by creating a greater sense of belonging and improving self-esteem, according to new research from Durham University Business School.
title: AI companions could help reduce loneliness, study finds

description: Hydrogen peroxide is used in many industrial processes, with several million tons of it being manufactured worldwide every year. Whereas the standard production method requires rare precious metals, chemists from Rutgers University–Newark in the US and the University of Bonn have now described an alternative technique that does away with these metals, making it potentially cheaper and more sustainable. Their findings have now been published in the journal Nature Communications. In the following interview, the authors describe the technology.
title: Q&A: Making hydrogen peroxide without using precious metals

description: Academic journals are flooded with papers. At publishing giant Elsevier, the number of submissions rose 56% in just three years—from 2.7 million in 2022 to 4.2 million in 2025. That's a lot more papers. And peer reviewers, who generally volunteer their time, were already stretched thin.
title: Can AI save peer review from AI?

description: The first data from a U.K.-built instrument heading to Mercury have provided observations of one of the brightest X-ray sources in the sky from aboard the ESA/JAXA BepiColombo spacecraft in the inner solar system.
title: Mercury-bound X-ray telescope delivers first images after eight years in space

description: Scientists have created hollow capsules with single openings that can selectively filter particles thanks to the turbulence in surrounding waters—at times, ingesting particles like PAC-MAN eating up dots.
title: 'PAC-MAN' capsules that gobble up particles in turbulent water show promise for filtration and drug delivery

description: Researchers are calling for lasting investment in healthy seas to support food security, protect coastlines and strengthen economic resilience.
title: Britain should treat healthy seas as essential infrastructure, say scientists

description: In an ordinary metal, electrons behave like well-defined particles that occasionally bump into imperfections or vibrations of the crystal. Many materials with strong electron–electron interactions, including the copper-oxide (cuprate) superconductors, break these rules. In these "strange metals," electrical resistance rises in a straight line with temperature over a very wide range. Electrons seem to lose their momentum at the fastest rate quantum mechanics allows, the so-called Planckian limit. What causes this is still an open question.
title: The secret of 'strange metals' may lie in quantum statistics, not collisions

description: If dark matter and dark energy were a part of our everyday lives, we would live in a perpetual state of dumbfoundedness. Imagine living in a world where 95% of the matter and energy were invisible and undetectable. It would be impossible to make sense of our surroundings.
title: Euclid's hunt for strong gravitational lenses is off to a strong start

description: Cattails are a familiar sight in wetlands, where they thrive in both brackish and freshwater marshes. But surviving in waterlogged soil presents a challenge; their roots need oxygen in an environment where very little is available.
title: Staying alive in marsh muck: The tiny 'snorkels' cattails grow manipulate soil chemistry

description: A research team led by professor Youhei Takeda at the University of Osaka, in collaboration with professor Zachary M. Hudson at the University of British Columbia (UBC) in Canada, has developed a polymer material that combines fluorescent cell imaging with the potential to kill cancer cells when activated by light. The material could offer a simpler approach to developing "nanotheranostic" technologies, which bring disease imaging and treatment together in a single platform.
title: Dual-purpose polymer dots could combine bioimaging and light-triggered cell death in one material

description: After meerkats emerge each morning from their burrow to warm in the early sun, there's one thing on their collective mind, and that's to find food. They navigate communally as they head off, working slowly along their route before returning home swiftly at the end of the day. But although the tight-knit band navigates as one, some members of the clan could be more experienced after roaming solo, shaping the community's maneuvers.
title: Individual meerkats are ace solo navigators

description: University of Michigan researchers have discovered a mechanism that enables microscopic organisms like bacteria and fungi to produce drug-like molecules—compounds that can fight infections or kill cancer cells—without damaging themselves.
title: How microbes make drug-like chemicals without damaging themselves

description: Around four years ago, humanity intentionally hit an asteroid. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) was by pretty much all measures a resounding success when it struck the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos going more than 22,000 kilometers per hour (13,700 miles per hour). However, we still don't know just how much of a success it actually was—DART was a one-way mission with no real way to track the results of the impact close up.
title: ESA's Hera probe uses 'superhuman' vision to inspect NASA's asteroid crash site

description: Scientists have hypothesized that, in the fraction of a second following the Big Bang, minute black holes may have been forged within tiny, dense pockets that collapsed under their own gravity. If these primordial black holes are ever found, they could represent a significant component of dark matter—the invisible substance that makes up most of the universe's matter.
title: If tiny 'primordial' black holes exist, here's how we might find them

description: Dr. Arthur Tiutenko from FAU and colleagues from LMU München and the South African National Museum in Bloemfontein discovered a new species of snake in the Harenna Forest, on the southern slopes of Ethiopia's Bale Mountains: Dasypeltis albigularis, or the white-throated egg-eater. "Three other new species in this genus are still waiting in line," the zoologist adds.
title: The snake with a built-in egg peeler

description: Tiny chemical marks on histones—the proteins that package our DNA—can profoundly influence gene activity without changing the underlying DNA sequence. One such mark, known as histone acetylation, plays a crucial role in regulating gene expression and is frequently disrupted in diseases such as cancer. Researchers, however, wondered how the enzymes responsible for adding these marks know exactly where to place them.
title: How a tiny chemical mark on a protein can be placed to double gene activity

description: Chronically lonely people are less likely to buy products that benefit others, such as fair-trade or child-labor-free goods, according to a new study by researchers at Concordia and the University of the Fraser Valley. The team ran four studies involving more than 1,400 participants across North America. Each person completed a standard loneliness questionnaire, then chose between ordinary products and versions that cost 15% to 20% more but carried an ethical or environmental label. Items included toothpaste, chocolate bars, jackets and backpacks.
title: Lonely shoppers demonstrate less compassion in their purchases than others, study shows

description: For patients with head and neck cancer, treatment can come at a high cost to their quality of life, affecting their ability to speak, swallow and even breathe due to invasive procedures. Now, Penn State researchers have developed a light-activated nanoparticle system with the long-term goal of shrinking tumors while limiting exposure to healthy tissue and improving patients' quality of life after cancer treatment. Penn State has licensed the technology to Illuminate Therapeutics, which is advancing its preclinical development.
title: Light-activated nanoparticles may help treat head and neck cancer

description: Experts were puzzled when satellite observations showed a volcano in Ethiopia emitting huge quantities of methane despite not erupting, but a team of researchers led by the University of Bristol believe they have discovered why this happened—and their findings could have implications for historical climate change research.
title: Ethiopian volcano's mysterious methane outburst may have a culprit—magma that never erupted

description: As Giving Tuesday approaches, a recent study led by a University of Massachusetts Amherst public policy researcher finds that communities with greater economic disadvantage typically see less private charitable giving—despite having greater needs in many cases.
title: Ahead of Giving Tuesday, study finds charitable giving often misses communities with greatest need

description: Mosquitoes play a major role in spreading malaria, and understanding how they adapt to climate change is important for improving malaria prevention and control.
title: Gene variant gives male malaria mosquitoes a mating edge in the heat

description: Though we may fight with our siblings sometimes, for most people a sibling is a constant companion throughout childhood and often for one's entire life. Yet this is not always the case in the animal kingdom: in some species, siblings engage in serious fights that can even escalate to fratricide. They may be genetically related, but must also compete for limited resources.
title: Cichlid sibling rivalry: Young fish fight more in some species than others

description: New research led by Dr. Stephen Agnew from Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury's (UC) Department of Economics and Finance is challenging one of the most persistent assumptions in education and everyday culture: that teenage girls are less financially literate than boys.
title: Rethinking the 'girls are worse with money' myth

description: The "motherhood penalty"—a workplace bias that assumes mothers are less committed to their careers, resulting in fewer opportunities, lower pay and slower advancement—could be reduced by shifting jobs from in-person to remote, according to new research by Claire Daviss, assistant professor of organizational behavior at the ILR School.
title: Remote jobs diminish hiring bias against mothers

description: Large, complex genomes remain difficult to characterize accurately, even with modern DNA sequencing. Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology have now extended an optical genome mapping approach, previously demonstrated for bacterial genomes, to more complex eukaryotic genomes. Using two yeast species, they generated optical maps covering entire chromosomes, including large repetitive regions that are particularly difficult to reconstruct.
title: Optical DNA mapping assembles yeast genomes at chromosome scale

description: Water, at least in its purest form, contains hydrogen and oxygen. In 1800, scientists first used electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen gases. Today, this process, known as water electrolysis, is widely used to produce hydrogen for industrial purposes, including manufacturing ammonia for agricultural fertilizers that sustain global food production.
title: Improving hydrogen production from water can support abundant global crops

description: A research team has traced how a molecule rearranges its electrons when excited by light. The findings, published in Angewandte Chemie International Edition, help clarify a long-standing question and open new possibilities for studying chemistry in motion, such as bonds breaking or forming—fundamental steps in reactions involving catalysts and biological molecules. The collaboration included Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin (HZB), the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Villigen, Switzerland, and European XFEL.
title: X-rays reveal fleeting intermediate step as iron-containing molecule responds to light

description: A park two miles (3.2 kilometers) from home might seem close enough for a Saturday outing. In metropolitan Detroit, though, park visits had already fallen to about half their modeled peak by that distance. In metropolitan Minneapolis, the same drop took nearly five miles (8 kilometers). And in the New York metropolitan area, with its extensive transit network, visitation fell by half at about 2.3 miles (3.7 kilometers). A park's reach, it turns out, depends a great deal on where it is.
title: New research explains how far people will go for a day at the park

description: Plant scientists know that what grows above the soil doesn't offer enough information to understand an entire plant community. Different species contribute differently to belowground biomass, and those differences matter for soil health and ecosystem functioning. However, digging up roots to separate and identify them by species, especially when many plants are growing together underground, can be difficult and time-consuming, according to a team of researchers in the College of Agricultural Sciences at Penn State.
title: Modified genetic method allows researchers to quantify roots growing underground

description: As they move and push against obstacles, cells generate forces. These forces originate in their internal skeleton, some parts of which behave like wool. This mechanical property has been revealed by scientists from the CNRS, Université Paris Cité and Université Paris-Saclay. This study is published in the journal Nature.
title: Cell skeleton networks stiffen like wool when compressed, experiments reveal

description: An international team of scientists has developed a method that can find pulsars in publicly available NASA data about a million times faster than before. This opens the door to discovering many more of these rapidly spinning objects. A paper describing the results was published in Physical Review Letters.
title: Cryptography-inspired method speeds up searches for elusive pulsars

description: Men outnumber women by four to one among performers booked at live music venues, but a new study by the University of Portsmouth has found no evidence that audiences systematically prefer male singing voices.
title: Music industry is tone-deaf to its own gender imbalance, experiments show

description: For Arctic researchers, counting beluga whales from the air can mean painstakingly examining thousands of aerial images—searching for animals that may be difficult to see and even harder to distinguish from one another. The challenge is especially significant when researchers are trying to identify calves, whose smaller size, lower numbers and variable appearance can make them easy to miss.
title: AI helps researchers track beluga whales using aerial drone images

description: Neanderthal DNA makes up about 2% of the genome of most non-Africans. When and how did that mixing take place, and what does it mean for modern humans?
title: Why do so many people have Neanderthal DNA?

description: Corporate CEOs are collecting enormous paychecks, even when their companies struggle to deliver results. New research from Case Western Reserve University suggests the problem isn't just how much executives earn; it's also how they're paid.
title: CEOs are getting richer, even when their companies aren't

description: Bacteria have many strategies for defending themselves against antibiotics. Some destroy the drug, others pump it out or alter its target. They can also, more simply, prevent it from getting in. A team at the University of Geneva (UNIGE) has discovered how Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a bacterium responsible for infections that are often difficult to treat, very rapidly restricts the entry of imipenem, an antibiotic reserved for the most critical cases. Published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, these findings reveal a mechanism of antibiotic resistance and open up new avenues for eventually counteracting it.
title: Pathogen P. aeruginosa uses protein to limit entry of last-resort antibiotic

description: Magnets are usually associated with a familiar property: they produce a magnetic field because the magnetic moments of their electrons align. But nature allows much more unusual forms of magnetic order. An international research team has now identified compelling experimental evidence for p-wave magnetism in europium silicide (EuSi), a chemically simple metallic compound.
title: Unusual magnetism revealed in a simple metal's electron spins

description: Michael Templeton is professor of public health engineering in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at Imperial College London and co-chair of the Imperial Global Development Lab Advisory Board. He holds the Oxfam and Water for People / Royal Academy of Engineering Research Chair in Global Sanitation Technology and is currently head of the environmental and water resource engineering section within the department.
title: How tiger worms could help tackle the global sanitation problem

description: When a U.S. airstrike struck Tehran's Arg Square on March 2, 2026, Golestan Palace was not the target. But it was close enough.
title: US and Iran once practiced diplomacy through archaeology—that legacy need not lie in ruins

description: More than 1,700 bee species are found only on islands, the first global checklist of island bees shows. If you like bees and island destinations, the best places to visit are in the Mediterranean. Islands like Sicily and Cyprus are where you find the highest diversity of bee species in the world. Bee connoisseurs will also appreciate large tropical islands like Hawaii and Madagascar, where they'll find unique bee species that live only on that particular island.
title: More than 1,700 bee species are unique to islands, first global assessment finds

description: NASA tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Nov. 18 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA's Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi.
title: NASA conducts latest RS-25 engine test in support of future Artemis missions

description: After centuries of whaling, humpback whales of the Southern Hemisphere were close to extinction. As few as 5,000 animals were left in the oceans. But after efforts to end whaling culminated in a 1985 moratorium, the whales began one of the biggest comebacks in conservation. Around 50,000 humpback whales now migrate along the eastern Australian coastline.
title: This year's humpback whale migration was missing something vital—the calves and their mothers

description: The rapid expansion of data centers for artificial intelligence causes negative health and air quality impacts in regions far from where the brick-and-mortar facilities are located, according to a new study by MIT researchers.
title: Data centers damage air quality long-distance, study reveals

description: Researchers Alessandra Buja and Sohail Akhtar at the University of Padova in Italy conducted a meta-analysis of studies looking at aging adults' quality of life in relation to spirituality and religiosity. Their findings, published Nov. 19 in the open-access journal PLOS Aging and Health, suggested that being religious or spiritual boosts one's view of one's life, and having faith generally confers a greater benefit than turning to it as a means of coping.
title: Spirituality and religiosity associated with better quality of life in older adults

description: A fleck-sized chip at the bottom of a test tube can provide researchers with data for every second of a chemical reaction while it is occurring.
title: Chips smaller than rice grains wirelessly track heat during chemical reactions

description: In the Federal Court of Australia, applications by self-represented litigants, many using artificial intelligence to research and draft their claims, have skyrocketed.
title: Why using a chatbot as your lawyer is a risky move—and ties up our court system

description: New research from the University of Aberdeen suggests weight-loss medications could deliver a double benefit, improving people's health while also helping the environment.
title: Weight-loss drugs could reduce deaths and ease pressure on agricultural land by 2050

description: The Cincinnati Zoo's animal care team has been working for days to help its beloved hippo Fiona safely digest and pass a knit cap she swallowed.
title: Cincinnati Zoo hopes a little shake will help Fiona the hippo pass a swallowed hat

description: An unassuming fossil discovery in Wyoming caused quite a stir: Was it a baby dinosaur, a prehistoric snake or perhaps an entirely new species? Neutron imaging at the Paul Scherrer Institute PSI and the trained eye of a paleontologist eventually provided the answer: the 156-million-year-old fossil is that of a previously unknown species of reptile.
title: Neutrons, death metal and a tiny prehistoric dragon: Scans reveal new horned reptile species from 156 million years ago

description: Several years ago, the U.S. economist Raj Chetty and his team at Harvard University analyzed billions of ties on Facebook in a bid to learn more about social mobility. Their findings highlighted an important link between cross-class friendship and social mobility. Specifically, they found that people from low-income backgrounds who have more friends from wealthier backgrounds tend to have better chances of earning more as adults.
title: Diplomacy, humor and avoidance—what we found when we investigated friendships across class divides

description: Human and animal digestive systems host vast communities of microorganisms, including bacteria and viruses. Some are harmful, others are beneficial, and many remain poorly understood. In a recent study, scientists found an entirely new group of viruses without even having to go anywhere near anyone's innards.
title: Newly discovered gut viruses offer clues to the origins of the smallpox virus family

description: The Tancat de la Pipa, an artificial wetland designed as a "green filter" for the Albufera de València, reduces microplastic pollution in the natural lagoon by 36%, according to research conducted by the Institute of Water and Environmental Engineering (IIAMA) at the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV) and the Faculty of Environmental Sciences and Engineering at Babe–Bolyai University in Romania published in the journal Applied Sciences.
title: Artificial wetland near Valencia traps 36% of incoming microplastics, study finds

description: Researchers at the Department of Paleontology at the University of Vienna compared fossil and modern ear stones of the black goby (Gobius niger) from the northern Adriatic Sea to reconstruct its growth history over the past 8,000 years. The surprising result: while body size remained remarkably stable in the past, today's black gobies grow faster and reach larger sizes—even as the Adriatic Sea is warming rapidly. The study is now published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B.
title: Black gobies are growing larger despite climate change

description: In modern electronics and computing, finding advanced materials that can efficiently move electrical charges without losing energy remains a critical scientific challenge. While traditional metals conduct electricity exceptionally well, researchers continually seek innovative hybrid materials that combine the design flexibility of chemistry with true metallic performance.
title: New metal-organic material combines metallic conductivity with promise for light-sensing electronics

description: For more than 15 years, the Italian duck-billed dinosaur Tethyshadros insularis has been reconstructed with one of the most unusual mouth structures among hadrosauroids. The tip of its upper jaw featured three forward-pointing bony projections on each side, long interpreted as exposed "spikes" or toothlike beak ornaments. However, a new study published in Royal Society Open Science reveals that this interpretation was incorrect.
title: Duck-billed dinosaur discovered in Italy had a birdlike beak hidden among its bizarre 'spikes'

description: Suppose you are in charge of your firm's commuting policy and, after some research, you determine that 57% of your colleagues drive to work. How would you communicate that number to coworkers?
title: Confirmed: Numbers tell, but language sells

description: Predicting how proteins interact inside a cell is essential to understanding how organisms function and why they differ from one another, yet experimental hurdles and the computational cost of analyzing millions of protein pairs make it impossible to explore complete interaction networks, particularly in understudied bacteria and organisms.
title: Decoding interactomes: Supercomputing predicts bacterial protein links from shared evolutionary patterns

description: Racial minorities facing federal drug charges have allegations of conspiracy added to their cases at higher rates than their white counterparts, as prosecutors seek to push them over the threshold for a mandatory minimum sentence that then can be used in negotiating stiffer penalties, a new UConn study finds.
title: Mandatory minimum sentencing oftentimes means 10 more months in prison, study finds

description: An international research team led by geologists from the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences (DEPS) at The University of Hong Kong (HKU) has uncovered new evidence of how the moon's largest impact basin, the South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin, formed and evolved over billions of years.
title: Lunar sample research yields new discoveries, revealing the history of the moon's largest impact basin

description: Ecosystems can buffer the impacts of climate change and humans for only so long before an ecological turning point is reached, a new study on Aotearoa New Zealand's extinct mātuhituhi—bush wren—has highlighted.
title: Museum specimens yield new subspecies of New Zealand bush wren decades after its extinction

description: Stopover sites are more than just places for migratory birds to rest and refuel. They also help birds adapt to climate change, according to research by Leiden ecologist Yali Si.
title: Why stopover sites are vital for migratory birds as spring arrives earlier

description: Inside electronic devices, electric current can gradually displace atoms within tiny metal connections, creating gaps or unwanted accumulations that eventually cause circuits to fail. This phenomenon, known as electromigration, has long been regarded as a reliability problem that engineers must work to prevent. Yet the ability of an electric current to move atoms also raises the possibility of putting that movement to constructive use, directing atoms through a material rather than allowing them to migrate uncontrollably.
title: From broken circuits to growing graphite: A new role for electromigration

description: One in 100 of the tiny particles hanging in the air we breathe in Michigan is a microplastic, according to a University of Michigan study. The study tested the air for microplastics in four locations across lower Michigan, all in the parking lots of K-12 schools. It found that microplastics constitute about 1% of particles found in the atmosphere.
title: Microplastics make up 1 in 100 airborne particles sampled at four Michigan schools

description: Australia's Safeguard Mechanism (SGM) is failing to reduce emissions and drive decarbonization in the industrial and mining sectors because of an overreliance on cheap, low-integrity offsets, according to a new report titled "Phantom Forests and the Safeguard Mechanism: How Low-integrity Offsets are Obstructing Climate Action."
title: Phantom forests: How low-integrity offsets lead to policy failure

description: Some personalities stand out on the first date and end up being asked for a second date, but not the ones we expect. While very few people want to date people with dark traits like psychopathy and sadism, they seem to make a good first impression. Psychopathy involves traits such as manipulation, low empathy and impulsivity, while sadism involves taking pleasure in others' suffering. Yet, on a first date, these traits don't necessarily stop someone from coming across as an appealing romantic partner.
title: Dark personality traits linked to better chance at getting a second date

description: Anger and frustration can run high in online discussions about climate change. But a new study led by Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) suggests that hostility in these conversations tends to follow earlier hostility, hinting that people may pick up uncivil behavior from others.
title: Hostility in online heat wave discussions shows signs of contagion, study suggests

description: Twenty years of weather radar observations around Darwin have helped researchers investigate a surprising feature of tropical rain: the fiercest local downpours tend to occur when the surrounding atmosphere is relatively dry.
title: Why fierce tropical downpours thrive in a relatively dry atmosphere

description: A research team including scientists from Ehime University successfully synthesized high-purity CeFeO3, a difficult-to-produce cerium–iron mixed oxide, using hydrogen reduction. By optimizing hydrogen concentration and gas flow rate, they achieved a phase purity of up to 99 mol%. The team also clarified the formation mechanism and identified factors that hinder synthesis. This method, published in the journal Inorganic Chemistry, provides a foundation for future research into applications in magnetic materials and catalysis.
title: Successful high-purity synthesis of the challenging-to-produce cerium orthoferrite!

description: Many people believe there are obvious ways to spot a liar without listening to a word they say, such as shifty glances and nervous fidgeting. Psychologists, however, are increasingly looking past these supposed telltale signs, which aren't necessarily reliable, toward subtler, involuntary clues that can be harder to detect.
title: Trying to hide some information? Your eyes might give you away

description: The European Chemicals Agency said Thursday that one of its expert committees was backing EU-wide restrictions on so-called "forever chemicals," citing risks to both the environment and health.
title: Key EU committee backs EU-wide restrictions on 'forever chemicals'

description: NASA's Voyager 1 has phoned home from one light-day away, humanity's first emissary to cross this monumental threshold way out in interstellar space.
title: NASA's Voyager 1 phones home from an awe-inspiring 1 light-day away

description: Astronomers have discovered a stellar system just 28 light-years from Earth that challenges our understanding of how stars live, die and interact as they evolve.
title: Astronomers discover remarkable triple-star system just 28 light-years from Earth

description: The severity of the flooding experienced by l'Horta Sud on Oct. 29, 2024, can be explained by a combination of exceptional rainfall, near-simultaneous rises in several ravines and a heavily urbanized area, according to a study carried out by the Institute of Water and Environmental Engineering at the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), which reconstructs the event using rainfall data and mathematical models capable of simulating how rain is transformed into runoff, how water carries sediment and how the flood spreads across the territory.
title: Study identifies factors that exacerbated the 2024 flash flood in l'Horta Sud

description: In living cells, tiny molecules can generate coordinated motion across distances thousands of times larger than the molecules themselves. How such small movements give rise to coordinated motion over much larger distances is still not fully understood.
title: Long DNA strands turn chaotic fluid motion into a steady rhythm

description: MBARI's advanced technologies continuously monitor the oceanographic and biological conditions in Monterey Bay. These instruments and the decades of data they have collected are invaluable as MBARI scientists work to understand how the historic 2026–2027 El Niño will affect marine life and ecosystems.
title: A blue desert: Researchers record decrease in phytoplankton in Monterey Bay due to El Niño

description: Researchers have discovered a physical effect that expands the fundamental understanding of how electric currents interact with magnetism, revealing an unexpected way to manipulate the magnetic state of antiferromagnetic materials. A research team led by Northwestern Engineering's Pedram Khalili has discovered what it calls octupole-driven spin-transfer torque (OTT). The effect allows an electrical current to manipulate the magnetic state of a class of materials called noncollinear antiferromagnets.
title: Unexpected spin effect lets electric currents switch antiferromagnets at room temperature

description: Food waste depends not only on what people do but also on how refrigerators and packaging are designed. This is the conclusion of a study from Linköping University (LiU) in Sweden. Information campaigns are not enough. Refrigerators and packaging must also be designed based on how people actually behave, according to the researchers.
title: Fridges and packaging contribute to food waste

description: A new study finds that a Brazilian policy aimed at reducing deforestation appears to be remarkably effective and has significantly reduced forest loss in the Brazilian Amazon. The largest reductions occurred on private lands specifically targeted by Brazil's Priority List (PL) policy, with no evidence that deforestation shifted to other land ownerships or neighboring municipalities.
title: Brazil's approach to deforestation delivers major reductions in Amazon forest loss

description: As solar power and batteries make it possible for homes to generate and store their own power, more Australians are wondering whether they need the power grid at all.
title: Secondhand solar, tiny houses, no bills—we found how Australians are going off‑grid and if it's worth it

description: A new study from NTNU's Industrial Ecology Programme examines the proportion of greenhouse gas emissions from transportation compared with food production.
title: What we eat matters more for the climate footprint than where it's grown

description: Psychiatric diagnoses are the most common cause of long-term sick leave in Sweden. Stress-related mental health problems and exhaustion disorder are the most common conditions. Women are affected more often than men.
title: Practical advice for managers when employees experience mental health problems

description: Duplexes, townhouses and small apartment buildings, often called mid-density housing, could help cities ease shortages and improve affordability. However, there is little data on how much of this housing exists. A new study by Yale School of the Environment scientists that focuses on Chicago found that it is widespread across the city, yet much of it sits in neighborhoods where current zoning doesn't allow that housing type.
title: AI maps overlooked housing to reveal gaps between Chicago's buildings and zoning rules

description: Researchers led by Professor Jinsung Park from the Department of Biomechatronic Engineering at Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU), have developed an ultrasensitive electrochemical sensor capable of detecting extremely low concentrations of vitamin C. By incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into the sensor development process, the research team identified promising fabrication conditions using a limited amount of experimental data, reducing the need for extensive trial-and-error optimization.
title: Researchers use AI to optimize sensor design for ultrasensitive vitamin C detection

description: Fiji and Tonga have declared that severe droughts fueled by the El Niño weather phenomenon are reaching crisis levels in the South Pacific.
title: Pacific island nations declare El Niño drought crisis

description: International experts are calling for marine heat waves to be tracked to inform strategies for sustaining fisheries and supporting communities reliant on oceans.
title: Call to improve global ocean monitoring to prepare for marine heat waves

description: One of the goals of gut microbiome research is that scientists will be able to develop treatments for various diseases that add or restore microbes with health benefits that are missing from the gut. This isn't as simple as just packing microbes into a probiotic capsule, though. Sometimes the most beneficial bacteria need a few tweaks before they can do their jobs.
title: New genetic toolkit lets scientists engineer hard-to-study gut bacteria

description: Father of four Adisorn Lakonburee used to catch fish for his family's dinner, but stopped after floodwaters brought oil slicks and foul chemical smells into his village in eastern Thailand.
title: Thai floods expose waste pollution in 'garbage dump' region

description: More than 100 million red crabs on Australia's Christmas Island have begun their annual migration from the forest to the sea, conservationists said this week.
title: Red crabs begin annual march to sea on Australia's Christmas Island

description: A single X‑ray photon can break both O–H bonds in a water molecule within a few femtoseconds (quadrillionths of a second), creating neutral atomic oxygen. As shown by a study published in the journal Physical Review Letters, this breakup happens before the electrons finish relaxing, revealing an ultrafast pathway for X‑ray–driven chemistry in water.
title: X-rays tear water apart before its electrons can relax

description: Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo's famed hippo, underwent a colonoscopy this week, and now veterinarians are trying a new way to help her pass a knit cap that she swallowed after it slipped into her enclosure.
title: Cincinnati Zoo trying to shake loose Fiona the hippo after she swallowed a hat

description: Researchers have shown that potatoes grown in simulated lunar soil amended with organic matter are safe to eat and can achieve growth and yields comparable to those produced on Earth. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," said Aymeric Goyer of Oregon State University's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology. "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon."
title: Potatoes grown in simulated lunar soil match Earth-grown performance
